construct: GNPTAB encodes the alpha and beta subunits of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase, which initiates synthesis of the mannose-6-phosphate recognition marker on lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi. Severe loss causes mucolipidosis II alpha/beta with failure of lysosomal enzyme targeting and extracellular mis-secretion of hydrolases.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Coarse facies, dysostosis multiplex, high plasma lysosomal hydrolases, low intracellular activity, and biallelic GNPTAB loss identify mucolipidosis II from failure to generate M6P lysosomal targeting markers.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Lysosomal acidification, LDL endocytosis, proteasomal ubiquitination, and autophagosome fusion do not explain extracellular mis-secretion of multiple lysosomal hydrolases from defective Golgi targeting.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The characteristic enzyme-distribution pattern and GNPTAB genotype uniquely identify the M6P-tagging defect.
